diagnosis.question: Can the v2 blade (120 x 40 x 1.5 mm, 25 deg double bevel) remove the TRIM-01-R dome at rho = 0-10 deg under cutting law 8, and what happens?
diagnosis.answer: Yes for the double bevel at rho = 5 and 10 deg (and 12.5/15 deg); no at rho = 0 deg. Every run is a separation outcome only; no run passes the full frozen 0.5 mm precision score (reported separately).
diagnosis.law8_regime: Below 15 deg law 8 never plowed (plowing_steps_last_substep = 0 for rho <= 15, including exactly 15 deg, where the float32 test tan^2 tie fell on the non-plowing side); rho = 25/35 plowed on every armed step. So rho = 0-15 ran pure law-4 labelling and still separated for the double bevel at 5-15 deg: concern (2) (a carried code-0 chip, which made law 4 fail TRIM at 25 deg) does not appear for the double bevel at these rakes: zero above-plane code-0 particles and zero direct code-0 bridges.

double_bevel_rho0_failure.outcome: FAIL_TRIM_SEPARATION: 70.3% removed (default controller), 87.0% (exact 0.2 mm clearance); substrate share 1.0, no code-0 bridges.
double_bevel_rho0_failure.mechanism_with_data: At rho = 0 the lower bevel face lies 0.75 mm below the edge (0.55 mm below the target plane) along the whole 40 mm blade body, which slides on the bar top (skim force 0.67 N mean vs 0.014 N at 5 deg). The pressed substrate and the dome base sink ahead of the edge before it arrives (median z displacement before labelling -0.36 mm vs -0.03 mm at 5 deg). The lowest above-plane layer (reference z = 20.5 mm, 0.1-0.3 mm above the edge) is then below the swept surface when the band labels it: 310 particles (29.7% of above-plane mass) get the lower-side digit (median height above the edge at labelling -0.14 mm) and stay with the substrate. Exact clearance (edge at 20.2 mm) still leaves 136 such particles. Precision shows the gouge separately: overcut 4.6% / 7.1% of the base (limit 1%), missing surface 3.8% / 6.3%.
double_bevel_rho0_failure.conclusion: Concern (1) is confirmed and is a separation failure, not only a gouge; it is geometric (bevel below the edge), not a law-8 gate effect.

chisel_failure.outcome: rho = 0 PASS (95.4%, 97.7% exact clearance); rho = 5 PASS at default (94.7%) but FAIL at exact clearance (0%); rho = 10 FAIL in all three runs (0%, repeated with the same seed and at exact clearance).
chisel_failure.mechanism_with_data: Each failure is one component held together by 1-3 above-plane code-0 particles (direct code-0 bridges 1-3). They come from the dome (reference z = 21.5 or 24.5 mm, x = -8.5 to +6 mm), are thrown ahead of the edge faster than it moves (about 40 vs 25 mm/s; f relative to the edge 2-30 mm) and never come behind the edge while armed (code0_diagnosis class never_behind_edge_while_armed = all). The law-4 band labels only material behind a moving segment, and law 8's lead rule (which labels 0 < f <= 2 dx ahead) is gated off because the motion is only 5-10 deg out of the blade plane. The TLMPM separation graph is on the REFERENCE stencil, so the stray particle's 4 mm reference stencil still shares nodes with both the digit-2 chip (about 410 particles) and digit-1 material (the lower-side z = 20.5 layer or the substrate). One code-0 particle therefore bridges the whole cut, wherever it ends up in space (two ended embedded at z = 7-9 mm near x = 75 mm).
chisel_failure.why_chisel_not_double: With the bevel on top, the chisel's upper (rake) face is inclined rho + 25 deg to the motion; the double bevel's is rho + 12.5 deg. Law 8's gate measures the motion against the blade plane (n_b), not against the face that pushes the chip, so the chisel at 5-10 deg plows like a 30-35 deg face while the gate sees 5-10 deg. Runs that separate under pure law-4 labelling all have a face at or below 27.5 deg (double rho 5-15, chisel 0); chisel 30 deg is marginal and 35 deg fails, consistent with law 4's TRIM failure at the v1 25 deg rake (face 37.5 deg).
chisel_failure.conclusion: The chisel does not help under law 8: it removes the bevel gouge but exposes the law-4 carried-particle failure because the plowing gate is blind to the face angle.

diagnosis.negative_controls: TRIM-02-K2-R05 (flat press on K2-R00): side push, no contact, stop mid-skim, lift-out mid-skim and half-length skim PASS. In both mid-skim withdrawals the 340 far-half particles stay 100% attached, no label lies beyond x_stop (max labelled x = -0.5 mm), and 0 labels are added while stopped, lifted or withdrawn. Flat press and blunt grip contact add no labels and keep one component, but FAIL their predeclared force-present checks: the press mean is 0.93 N against a 1 N level (the first 15 of 40 press steps cross the 3 mm air gap; 1.4-1.9 N in contact, 1.55 N hold). The grip mean is 0.033 N against 0.1 N (95/124 steps in contact, max 0.079 N; a 3 mm bulldoze of the dome top). Neither threshold is changed. The resumed stop-mid skim also separates (97.7%).
diagnosis.controller_note: The formal runs use the frozen WaypointPolicy 0.5 mm position tolerance (as matrix M3a). The armed edge therefore starts at 20.44 mm and descends to 20.2 mm across the pass (mu = -0.16 deg; about 20.3 mm over the dome). The supplementary tol10um runs hold the edge at exactly target + 0.2 mm. Both are reported; the verdicts differ only for chisel rho = 5.
diagnosis.precision_note: Precision is reported separately and is not part of the outcome. p95 plane error is 0.51-0.57 mm in every run (limit 0.5 mm), so no run passes the full frozen precision score. Overcut is about 0.95-1.03% for the passing double-bevel runs (limit 1%). The frozen maximum_gouge_depth_m reads 16-20 mm in several runs, including the passing ones and the v1 law-8 M3a baseline (0.02 m). It comes from individual surface columns and is not a physical gouge: the substrate top-layer depression from particle centres has a median of -0.13 mm in every run.
diagnosis.recommendation: Under law 8 as it is, use ruler_knife_v2_y (double bevel) at rho = 5-10 deg with the edge at target + 0.2 mm. Both clearance conditions pass (96.6/97.9% at 5 deg, 95.7/97.9% at 10 deg), with no code-0 bridges, a same-seed repeat (5 deg _002) with identical removal and above-plane code counts and every separation-relevant negative control clean. Prefer 10 deg for the live run if C2 reachability allows: the lowest blade point is 0.05 mm above the target, versus 0.25 mm below it at 5 deg. Do not use rho = 0 with the double bevel (bevel interference) or the chisel at rho >= 5 deg under law 8. A gate defined on the rake-face angle, or any new law, is a coordinator decision; nothing was changed or tuned here.
diagnosis.not_done: No live/Native run, no Lab, no IK/reachability (that is C2). Single seed (42) only, with one same-seed repeat of K2-R05 and K2C-R10. Provisional, uncalibrated material.
